marketRegime.rationale: US PCE at 3.8% YoY and Korea rate hike signal persistent inflation; offsetting Asian growth upgrades and stabilized commodity volatility support equilibrium positioning.

executivePulse.title: US inflation persistence
executivePulse.text: October PCE recorded 3.8% YoY; Fed policymakers report disagreement on inflation drivers per Reuters. Maintains pressure on December rate decision; no cut implied.

executivePulse.title: Iberia real estate rebound
executivePulse.text: Three Iberian cities ranked among Europe's top-10 most-sought markets for 2027 per Euronews, signalling capital rotation into Southern Europe assets amid rate stabilisation.

executivePulse.title: Asia-Pacific growth upgrade
executivePulse.text: Bank of Korea raised 2027 GDP forecast to 4.1% and 2026 to 3.9%, lifting base rate 25bp to 3.25% amid AI chip strength per Reuters and Yonhap. Underpins EM tech allocation.

houseView.label: Spain & Madrid Real Estate
houseView.change: Three Iberian cities named among Europe's top-10 property investment targets for 2027 per Euronews; Prologis acquiring major Barcelona industrial site signals institutional capital inflow. Core market positioning justified.

houseView.label: European Credit & Financing
houseView.change: No material shifts in EU financing conditions this cycle. ECB October meeting rhetoric unchanged; euro credit spreads stable. Rate environment remains constraining for marginal credits.

houseView.label: Private Capital Deployment
houseView.change: PE deal velocity mixed: Ares funds $1.3B windshield buyout and Airbus satellites to Cerberus, but Mexico FDI collapsed 50% YoY Q3 per BNamericas; Asia data-centre investment set to decelerate per Fitch due to US chip curbs. Sector-level dispersion persists.

houseView.label: Energy & Commodities
houseView.change: Iran LNG vessel mine strike revived Hormuz supply concerns; oil prices rebounded from 3-month lows per OilPrice.com. Citi projects Q1 2027 prices at $60–65/bbl. Geopolitical tail-risk embedded; fundamentals moderating.

houseView.label: Emerging Markets
houseView.change: Bank of Korea 2027 growth forecast raised to 4.1%; rate hike to 3.25% signals confidence in AI-led expansion per Reuters/Yonhap. Offsets Mexico FDI weakness and India–UK trade deal stall; Asia tech growth differentiator intact.

houseView.label: Global Risk Appetite
houseView.change: US tariff proposals create bilateral negotiation risk (India, South Korea cited); PCE inflation at 3.8% constrains rate-cut expectations. Korean growth upgrade and Iberian asset strength provide modest countercyclical ballast.

catalysts.title: US Thanksgiving break market closure (partial liquidity)

globalBriefing: Korean growth upgrade to 4.1% (2027) and 25bp rate hike signal Asia-Pacific tech momentum diverging from US sticky inflation (PCE 3.8% YoY), creating asymmetric EM carry opportunities; however, Mexico FDI collapse (−50% YoY) and multilateral US tariff proposals compress LatAm and trade-exposed EM allocations. Iberian real-estate leadership and Barcelona industrial capex (Prologis) reaffirm Southern Europe capital rotation, anchoring Spain constructive stance amid modest geopolitical oil volatility (Hormuz incident) offsetting Citi's $60–65/bbl Q1 outlook.
marketOpen: Monitor Korea and India tariff negotiation signals; watch for US tariff proposal implementation timeline as primary regime determinant for EM credit repricing and cross-border deal timing.

macro.label: Macro & Central Banks
macro.description: Central bank decisions, inflation prints, GDP, yield curves, and FX

items.headline: US PCE inflation at 3.8% YoY in October; Fed policymakers divided on inflation causes
items.summary: October PCE recorded 3.8% year-over-year per Kotak Neo; Reuters reports Fed officials at odds on underlying drivers. No new policy signals issued; December meeting timing remains uncertain.
items.relevance: Sustains expectations of elevated near-term rates; delays market repricing of terminal rate expectations and extends duration headwinds for leveraged credit.

items.headline: Bank of Korea raises base rate to 3.25% (+25bp) and upgrades 2027 GDP to 4.1%, 2026 to 3.9%
items.summary: Per Reuters, Yonhap News Agency and Seeking Alpha, BOK lifted rates to highest level in two years amid AI chip sector strength and upgraded both 2026 and 2027 growth forecasts. Rate cycle acceleration signals regional monetary tightening shift.
items.source: Reuters, Yonhap News Agency, Seeking Alpha
items.relevance: Reinforces divergence between EM tech-driven growth (Korea) and US disinflation delays; raises cost of capital for regional leveraged finance and signals confidence in Asia-Pacific cyclical recovery.

items.headline: US Q3 GDP growth robust; October inflation remains elevated
items.summary: Per Reuters, US economy recorded strong third-quarter expansion but inflation persisted into October. Data confluence supports 'growth with sticky inflation' regime rather than soft-landing narrative.
items.relevance: Reinforces stagflationary tilt; maintains pressure on real yields and complicates Fed exit strategy. Benefits hard assets and commodities while pressuring leveraged equities.

macro.keyTakeaway: If US inflation remains above 3.5% and Fed messaging remains hawkish through December, expect extended US real rate premium to widen, pressuring EM carry and high-yield refinancing through Q1 2027.

geopolitics.label: Geopolitics & Security
geopolitics.description: Conflicts, alliances, sanctions, and power shifts

items.headline: LNG carrier reportedly struck mine in Strait of Hormuz; Iranian IRGC claims vessel was transiting 'illegal' route
items.summary: Per OilPrice.com, Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps reported an LNG vessel caught fire after striking a naval mine in Hormuz. Oil prices rebounded from three-month lows on renewed supply disruption concerns. No casualty or spill figures confirmed.
items.relevance: Reintroduces geopolitical tail-risk to crude markets; Hormuz chokepoint stress amplifies volatility in energy complex. Affects long-duration infrastructure financing in Middle East and raises insurance costs for shipping.

items.headline: Foreign Affairs reports EU entering period of political instability that could erode capacity to act
items.summary: Analytical piece from Foreign Affairs warns of gradual institutional degradation within EU rather than formal dissolution; highlights fragmentation risks across member states. No quantified data or formal policy announcement.
items.relevance: Structural concern for eurozone credit spreads and cross-border capital allocation confidence; signals elevated political-event risk around EU fiscal coordination and regulatory harmonisation.

items.headline: BBC reports diesel tanker with up to 7,000 tonnes sank near Ibiza; environmental damage being assessed
items.summary: Per BBC World, vessel carried up to 7,000 tonnes diesel; Spain's sea rescue service assessing environmental impact. One fatality reported. Direct operational impact limited; spill risk to Mediterranean logistics and tourism infrastructure.
items.relevance: Localized Mediterranean environmental and insurance cost event; minor relevance to broader ZRC mandate unless spill triggers EU maritime regulation tightening.

geopolitics.keyTakeaway: If Hormuz transit friction persists and EU political cohesion weakens further, expect higher crude volatility (oil risk premium +3–5%), lower eurozone credit quality, and capital flight toward USD-denominated EM credit.

fdi.label: FDI & Capital Flows
fdi.description: Cross-border investments, sovereign wealth, and capital movements

items.headline: Foreign direct investment in Mexico plunges almost 50% in third quarter YoY
items.summary: Per BNamericas, Mexico recorded near 50% decline in FDI inflows in Q3 2026 compared to prior year. No detailed sector breakdown provided; timing coincides with tariff policy uncertainty signals.
items.relevance: Critical headwind for nearshoring thesis and North American supply-chain resilience narratives; signals capital hesitancy on USMCA stability amid Trump tariff proposals. Affects LatAm credit spreads and EM allocations.

items.headline: US chip export curbs will slow Asia data-centre investment, Fitch cautions
items.summary: Per Reuters/Fitch, US semiconductor export restrictions are expected to decelerate data-centre capex in Asian markets. Contradicts near-term AI-driven infrastructure rally narrative. Timing horizon for slowdown unspecified.
items.relevance: Caps upside for Korean and Southeast Asian data-centre and infrastructure equity/debt; pressures tech-sector earnings growth in Asia. Supports cautious stance on EM tech-focused private capital deployment.

items.headline: Australia data-centre investment surge driven by AI demand; largest business investment increase since mining boom
items.summary: Per Reuters, Australian business investment jumped notably, anchored by data-centre capex boom tied to AI infrastructure demand. Counterpoint to Asia slowdown signals; Australia positioned as chip-curb-resistant jurisdiction.
items.relevance: Opens relative-value opportunity for Australian infrastructure and tech assets; underscores geographic fragmentation in AI capex deployment across Asia-Pacific. Supports selective EM infrastructure plays.

items.headline: India–UK investment treaty negotiations stall; bilateral pact unlikely soon, officials say
items.summary: Per Reuters, India–UK investment treaty talks have stalled; officials cite low probability of near-term resolution. Timing for resumption not provided.
items.relevance: Delays liberalisation of UK–India capital flows and reduces bilateral trade financing certainty. Minor direct impact given portfolio concentration, but signals broader EM–DM capital structure fragmentation.

fdi.keyTakeaway: If Mexico FDI weakness persists and US chip curbs expand, nearshoring thesis retreats and capital rotates toward Australia, UAE, and select DM infrastructure; EM ex-Asia alternative asset returns compress.

critical-minerals.label: Commodities & Energy
critical-minerals.description: Oil, gas, metals, supply chains, and energy security

items.headline: Oil prices rebound from three-month lows as Hormuz supply concerns resurface
items.summary: Per OilPrice.com, January WTI recovered mid-week as Middle East supply fears returned after earlier decline on volume concerns. No specific price levels or bps moves quantified in headline.
items.relevance: Restores oil geopolitical risk premium; supports long energy positions and inflationary bias for commodities allocation. Affects hedging costs for corporates with Middle East exposure.

items.headline: Citi projects oil prices trending lower to $60–65/bbl by Q1 2027
items.summary: Per EnergyNow.com citing Citi research, medium-term crude outlook revised downward to $60–65/bbl range in first quarter 2027. Reflects supply/demand balance skepticism offsetting geopolitical risk premium.
items.relevance: Signals medium-term energy deflation expectations; pressures EM fiscal revenues and long-duration energy credit. Supports cost-inflation moderation narrative for manufacturing and transport.

items.headline: Turkmenistan TAPI gas pipeline nears major milestone; key section expected to supply Afghanistan by early 2027
items.summary: Per OilPrice.com, Turkmenistan reports $10 billion TAPI pipeline project advancing toward early 2027 supply commencement to Afghanistan's third-largest city, despite multi-year delays. Completion timing remains subject to execution risk.
items.relevance: Long-term Asia energy diversification play reducing Middle East chokepoint dependency; supports Central Asian infrastructure credit and regional stability narratives. Timing uncertainty limits near-term deployment impact.

items.headline: TEPCO delays restart of second reactor at Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, world's largest nuclear plant, citing unspecified issues
items.summary: Per OilPrice.com, Tokyo Electric Power deferred reactor restart at Kashiwazaki-Kariwa (global nameplate capacity leader) on technical grounds. Timing for restart not disclosed.
items.relevance: Extends Japan's energy import dependency and supports LNG/crude demand. Delays nuclear cost-deflation narrative for Asia power markets; pressures regional energy security risk premium.

items.headline: Libya plans oil bidding rounds in 2027 and 2028 despite mounting security risks
items.summary: Per OilPrice.com, Libyan authorities scheduled exploration bidding rounds for developed and undeveloped fields in 2027–2028 to ramp production, acknowledging persistent instability. Execution risk high; production timeline uncertain.
items.relevance: Signals medium-term global supply growth intent but subject to geopolitical event risk; supports long-cycle energy thesis contingent on North Africa stability. Limited near-term capital allocation clarity.

critical-minerals.keyTakeaway: If geopolitical supply shocks persist (Hormuz) but fundamental supply/demand balance weakens, oil volatility expands while mean price drifts toward $60–65/bbl, favoring oil volatility derivatives over directional longs.

real-estate.label: Real Estate & Infrastructure
real-estate.description: Institutional RE, infrastructure projects, and market trends

items.headline: Three Iberian cities ranked among Europe's top-10 property investment targets for 2027
items.summary: Per Euronews and Yahoo Finance Singapore, three cities in Spain and Portugal identified as among Europe's ten most-sought investment destinations for 2027. No specific cities, capital flows or valuations quantified.
items.relevance: Signals institutional capital rotation toward Southern Europe real estate amid rate stabilisation and fiscal coordination expectations. Supports constructive stance on Madrid/Iberian logistics and residential plays. Directly reinforces Spain & Madrid RE positioning.

items.headline: Prologis acquires site for major Barcelona industrial hub
items.summary: Per CoStar, logistics REIT Prologis completed acquisition of property for significant Barcelona industrial development. Deal size, timing and rental yield assumptions not disclosed.
items.relevance: Institutional capital affirmation of Barcelona logistics market strength; signals conviction in Iberian supply-chain resilience and e-commerce infrastructure. Supports European logistics REIT allocations.

items.headline: EBRD backs landmark water desalination project in Jordan
items.summary: Per EBRD, development bank approved backing for major water desalination infrastructure in Jordan. Project scale, capital amount and timeline not detailed.
items.relevance: Signals multilateral support for MENA critical infrastructure; affects long-term water/energy nexus investment thesis and regional credit quality perceptions. Limited direct European real-estate relevance.

items.headline: Castlelake's Europe CRE head pivots strategy toward credit
items.summary: Per Green Street News, Castlelake Europe commercial real-estate leadership signals strategic shift from equity to credit-focused positioning. Underlying rationale and capital reallocation quantum not specified.
items.relevance: Tactical insight on European CRE capital structure preferences amid higher rates; suggests equity-valuation caution and debt-opportunity openness. Supports cautious equity stance, selective debt positioning in European real estate.

real-estate.keyTakeaway: If Iberian investor sentiment sustains and Barcelona logistics capex accelerates, Spanish real-estate credit spreads may tighten 20–40bps while equity cap rates stabilise, justifying constructive private capital allocation to logistics and residential plays.

ma-growth.label: M&A & Private Capital
ma-growth.description: Deal flow, PE/VC activity, and corporate transactions

items.headline: Ares funds $1.3 billion debt for buyout of windshield firm Cary
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Ares Capital arranged $1.3 billion in debt financing for acquisition of Cary windshield manufacturing. No LBO entry multiple, expected return or strategic buyer ID disclosed.
items.relevance: Signals continued PE debt capital availability for mid-market industrial buyouts; supports cautious constructive view on PE deployment in stable, cash-generative sectors. Smaller-scale transaction suggests deal flow normalisation.

items.headline: Airbus sells US satellite business to private equity firm Cerberus
items.summary: Per Aerospace Testing International, Airbus completed divestiture of US satellite operations to PE acquirer Cerberus. Deal valuation, strategic rationale and cash deployment not provided.
items.relevance: Strategic divest by large industrial; signals PE appetite for defence-adjacent space infrastructure. Suggests portfolio consolidation by defence primes and PE confidence in long-duration government contracting. Supports EM infrastructure optionality.

items.headline: Premier Partners to acquire Korea Fund Partners at $475 million valuation
items.summary: Per KED Global, PE firm Premier Partners agreed to purchase Korea Fund Partners at $475 million enterprise valuation. No earnout, sector focus, or deployment timeline specified.
items.relevance: Signal of PE capital migration toward Asia-Pacific fund management; small-scale GP consolidation play. Supports thesis of Asia PE capital concentration amid regulatory fragmentation.

items.headline: Independent sponsors emerging as growth phase driver in PE landscape
items.summary: Per PEI Private Equity, independent sponsor model identified as next-phase growth vector in private equity. No data on capital committed, deal volume or return benchmarks provided.
items.relevance: Structural commentary on PE capital fragmentation away from mega-managers; affects fundraising velocity for traditional GP platforms and pressures LPA return expectations. Supports selective private capital deployment thesis.

items.headline: Buyout firms targeting Global Payments; multiple bidders reported
items.summary: Per Digital Transactions, Global Payments identified as target for leveraged buyout interest; bidders implied but not named. Deal process stage, valuation expectations and financing terms unconfirmed.
items.relevance: Signals PE appetite for systemically important fintech/payments infrastructure amid regulatory clarity; supports constructive private capital deployment in scale businesses with recurring revenue. Headline unconfirmed.

ma-growth.keyTakeaway: If deal leverage remains accessible and strategic divestitures continue (Airbus model), mid-market PE deployment sustains; Mexico FDI collapse and China ODI records suggest geographic consolidation toward developed markets and selected EM tech hubs.

emerging-markets.label: Emerging Markets
emerging-markets.description: Frontier opportunities, risk signals, and market access

items.headline: Bank of Korea raises 2027 GDP growth forecast to 4.1%, 2026 to 3.9%; rate hike to 3.25%
items.summary: Per Reuters, Yonhap and Seeking Alpha, BOK upgraded dual-year growth outlook and lifted benchmark rate by 25bp to highest level in two years, citing AI chip sector strength. Monetary tightening acceleration signals confidence in structural growth.
items.source: Reuters, Yonhap News Agency, Seeking Alpha
items.relevance: Reinforces divergence between tech-led EM growth (Korea) and US disinflation delays. Strengthens KRW carry appeal and supports Korean equity/credit positioning within EM allocations. Pressures cost of capital for regional leveraged finance.

items.headline: India's state-owned gas company seeks investment partner for data-centre project
items.summary: Per Data Center Dynamics, Indian state utility NTPC seeks partner to develop data-centre infrastructure. Investment scale, timeline and technology partners unspecified.
items.relevance: Signals India's data-centre infrastructure gap and state-led capex intent; supports long-term India cloud/AI infrastructure thesis. Limited immediate capital deployment clarity; subject to US chip curb impact.

items.headline: Mexico FDI plunges almost 50% in Q3 YoY amid policy uncertainty
items.summary: Per BNamericas, Mexico recorded near-50% YoY decline in foreign direct investment in third quarter. Sector-level breakdown and forward guidance absent; timing coincides with US tariff policy signals.
items.relevance: Critical headwind for LatAm allocation; signals capital hesitancy on nearshoring thesis and North American trade regime stability. Pressures LatAm credit spreads and equity valuations.

items.headline: India faces choice on lower tariffs amid rushed US trade deal negotiations
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, India navigating tariff liberalisation pressure from US bilateral negotiations amid compressed timeline. India's negotiating position and expected outcomes unspecified.
items.relevance: Signals EM trade regime uncertainty and bilateral bargaining fragmentation replacing multilateralism. Affects India equity/credit risk premium and policy credibility. Supports cautious EM stance absent clarity.

items.headline: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on major US trading partners; Asia disproportionately exposed
items.summary: Per NPR, Reuters and CNBC, US tariff proposal wave targets multiple jurisdictions; Reuters/Korea Herald report South Korea specifically cited for industrial policy targeting. Scale of proposed rates and implementation timeline unspecified.
items.relevance: Reintroduces bilateral trade regime risk to EM capex/M&A confidence; pressures corporate earnings guidance in export-dependent sectors. South Korea and India disproportionately exposed. Supports cautious EM stance.

items.headline: Brazil positioned for increased weight in global emerging market portfolios
items.summary: Per Valor International, Brazil identified as candidate for portfolio reweighting within EM indices. No valuation data, capital flows or timeline specified.
items.relevance: Tactical insight on EM portfolio rebalancing; LatAm equity/credit demand thesis dependent on Mexico stability recovery. Limited immediate allocation guidance absent Brazil-specific catalysts.

emerging-markets.keyTakeaway: If Korean growth momentum sustains and US tariff proposals retreat, EM tech-led (Korea, India) outperformance vs. trade-exposed LatAm widens; Mexico FDI collapse and India tariff pressure compress LatAm/India allocations through Q1 2027.

trade-policy.label: Trade & Industrial Policy
trade-policy.description: Tariffs, sanctions, export controls, and economic statecraft

items.headline: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major US trading partners
items.summary: Per NPR, Trump administration rolled out fresh tariff proposals targeting core US trading partners. Specific rates, sectoral focus and timeline for implementation not disclosed.
items.relevance: Reintroduces bilateral trade regime uncertainty; pressures EM capex confidence and corporate earnings guidance across export-dependent sectors. Affects cross-border M&A/FDI timing and structuring.

items.headline: South Korea specifically cited by US for industrial policy targeting; Korea stands by policy post-tariff proposals
items.summary: Per Korea Herald and Business Korea, US administration flagged South Korea's Honam chip cluster industrial policy as concern; Seoul reaffirmed commitment to sector support. Bilateral negotiating stance hardening.
items.relevance: Signals potential US–Korea bilateral trade friction over subsidies/IP policy; pressures Korean equity valuations and cross-border tech M&A timing. Affects long-duration Korea semiconductor allocation.

items.headline: US tariff-hike threats pile pressure on trading partners to sign accelerated trade deals
items.summary: Per CNBC, US tariff proposals deployed as negotiating leverage to accelerate bilateral trade agreement closures. No specific deal targets, timelines or rate concessions quantified.
items.relevance: Signals bilateral deal compression and reduced multilateral coordination; affects regulatory/tariff certainty premiums across EM and DM exporters. Creates tactical deal-timing risk for cross-border capital flows.

items.headline: Trump's proposed tariff rates would restore levels from before Supreme Court intervention
items.summary: Per Yahoo Finance, proposed tariff schedules would reinstate pre-court-intervention rate levels, suggesting structural policy reversal. Specific rates and affected sectors not provided.
items.relevance: Signals durable tariff regime shift rather than temporary negotiating posture; affects long-duration trade-exposed corporate earnings and supply-chain investment decisions. Pressures EM export-dependent credit.

items.headline: India proposes US tariff comparison analysis amid bilateral trade deal negotiations
items.summary: Per Reuters, India is quantifying US tariff proposals relative to other trading partners as part of bilateral negotiation strategy. No India-specific tariff rates or concessions disclosed.
items.relevance: Signals India leveraging comparative tariff analysis to secure negotiating advantage; affects India–US deal timeline and bilateral relationship stability. Supports cautious India allocation stance.

trade-policy.keyTakeaway: If US tariff proposals advance and bilateral deals compress timelines, export-dependent EM credit (Mexico, India, Korea) reprices higher, nearshoring thesis retreats, and cross-border M&A timing risk elevated through Q1 2027.

food-agriculture.label: Food & Agriculture
food-agriculture.description: Food security, agribusiness, and agricultural commodities

items.headline: Corn and soybeans rally on pre-holiday technical buying and China demand signals
items.summary: Per AgWeb and AgroLatam, grain complex rallied on technical factors and reported increase in Chinese import signals ahead of holiday period. No specific prices, volume or Chinese purchase commitments quantified.
items.relevance: Signals tactical grain volatility and China demand elasticity; pressures feed/livestock margins and downstream agricultural credit. Supports commodity volatility positioning but limited structural impact.

items.headline: US soybean processing capacity threatens USDA's record production forecast
items.summary: Per AgroLatam, crushing capacity constraints are flagged as risk to USDA's elevated output forecast, implying structural supply/demand mismatch. No capacity figures or margin impact quantified.
items.relevance: Signals potential soybean supply-chain bottleneck and processing margin compression; affects agricultural credit risk and export revenues in grain-producing regions. Supports cautious agricultural commodity stance.

items.headline: ENOUGH Food weighs future of mycoprotein plant; production challenges force operational rethink
items.summary: Per AgFunder News, alternative protein producer ENOUGH Food reassessing mycoprotein plant viability due to industrial-scale production challenges and cost economics. No facility closure date or redeployment plan disclosed.
items.relevance: Signals operational/capital efficiency challenges in alt-protein scale-up; affects venture capital deployment confidence in category and food-tech exit timing. Supports cautious alt-protein allocation thesis.

items.headline: Zimbabwe imposes raw lithium export ban; processing capacity bottleneck constrains implementation
items.summary: Per African Business, Zimbabwe government restricts unprocessed lithium exports to incentivise domestic refining; mining operators report insufficient local processing capacity to absorb banned volumes. Policy-execution risk elevated.
items.relevance: Signals emerging-market resource nationalism and supply-chain structural risk; affects lithium price inflation and global battery supply-chain margins. Pressures EV transition capex assumptions.

food-agriculture.keyTakeaway: If soybean processing constraints bind and Zimbabwe lithium policy enforcement proceeds, commodity margins compress for agri-processors and battery supply tightens, pressuring agricultural credit and clean-tech financing through 2027.
